news.title: NY failed to disclose what it knew on 'toxic air' after 9/11

In the years since, more than 9,400 have died from illnesses linked to their exposure to the area, according to a federal medical monitoring program.

news.title: 12 countries including France, UK and Canada to sanction Israeli settlements

The action follows weeks of increasing attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the illegally occupied territory that has drawn widespread condemnation from the international community.

Washington has been pushing for fresh face-to-face talks between Moscow and Kyiv.

In conversation with FRANCE 24’s Stuart Norval, she talks about her book “Users – How big tech took control and How to Fight back”.

Some of them travelled from Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region to testify.

He depicts Yemen as moving from a prolonged condition of unresolved conflict into renewed regional confrontation. The relative calm established after 2022, he argues, never amounted to a durable political settlement: Yemen remains divided between rival political, financial and military institutions.

news.summary: El Tribunal General de la Unión Europea (TGUE) ha desestimado este miércoles el recurso presentado por el magnate ruso Roman Abramovich, expropietario del club inglés de fútbol Chelsea FC, contra la prórroga de las sanciones de la Unión Europea por la invasión de Ucrania al considerar probados sus vínculos económicos con el Kremlin y que las medidas restrictivas en su contra son "precisas y proporcionadas".

news.title: Houthis report Saudi reprisals after oil sites set ablaze in wave of strikes
news.summary: The Houthis said Saudi Arabia retaliated with strikes on Tuesday after the group targeted oil facilities, wounding dozens, as deadly fighting reignited in Yemen after a Houthi offensive towards the Red Sea's Bab al-Mandab chokepoint. The rapid round of strikes and counter-strikes follows the unravelling of a four-year truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government in July.

news.title: War in the Middle East: Iran attacks US base in Jordan, 10 US vessels
news.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they pummelled a US military base in Jordan, vowing retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers that dragged the foes deeper into war. Tehran's bombs came after US forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to Iran targeting an American warship, the second such attack in less than a week. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah reports from Tehran, Iran.

news.title: Diplomatic row escalates as UK, France and Canada move to sanction Israeli settlements
news.summary: Britain, France and Canada said Tuesday they will ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, with a UK minister accusing Israel of turning a blind eye to the "ethnic cleansing" of Palestinians there. The moves prompted a furious Israel to unveil immediate counter-measures targeting Britain, as Jerusalem-based journalist Jordana Miller reports.

news.title: FRANCE 24 report reveals Russia’s war on Ukraine’s books and cultural identity
news.summary: In Ukraine, the war is not being fought solely on the battlefield. This summer, Russian strikes severely affected the publishing industry, destroying dozens of warehouses and logistics centres. Millions of books and textbooks have been lost. For many Ukrainians, these attacks are part of an effort to erase their linguistic and cultural identity, as FRANCE 24’s Yegor Terletzkyi and Emmanuelle Chaze report.

news.title: Albanian anger undiminished after 100 days of protests against Kushner project
news.summary: Police in Albania blocked protesters from reaching parliament on Tuesday at the latest rally against a luxury development linked to US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Dubbed the ‘flamingo revolution’ for protesters’ signs depicting the pink bird that could be harmed by the coastal development, the protests are aimed at stopping the massive project that critics say would cause environmental damage and limit public access to the coast.

news.title: How France fell in love with Céline Dion
news.summary: Two years after her dazzling performance atop the Eiffel Tower for the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, Céline Dion is back in the French capital for a series of sold-out concerts – and fans are over the moon. Some 500,000 people are expected to attend the concerts.

news.title: US Rubio pledges to 'restore' ties with Colombia's new, Trump-friendly leader
news.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday pledged to "restore" ties with Bogota after four years of leftist rule, on day one of a three-nation tour aimed at bolstering conservative allies in Latin America. The trip to Colombia, Ecuador and Peru comes after a series of elections brought pro-US right-wing leaders to power, giving Washington an opening to tighten security and economic ties and push back against China's growing influence. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle tells us more.

news.title: Ballon d'Or: Dembélé, Kane and Mbappé among shortlisted stars

news.title: Hormuz impasse deepens: Iran retaliates against US targets after its oil tankers destroyed
news.summary: Iran launched fresh attacks against US targets in the Middle East on Wednesday in retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers, dragging the foes deeper into war. Tehran's powerful Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they attacked 20 US vessels trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for the world's oil and gas that Iran has largely controlled since the war erupted. The United States and Iran are locked in a stalemate six months into the war, with Iran maintaining a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz and Washington pushing a campaign to choke Iran's ports and economy.

news.title: JNIM jihadists step up incursions into northern Benin
news.summary: Al Qaeda affiliate JNIM has been intensifying its activities in Benin since 2022. The country serves as a transit corridor between the areas of operation of the group, which is well established in Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso. Two nature reserves have become logistical hubs for the jihadist fighters. Benin's army is striving to hold the line.
